summary: Most of the hardware humanity left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space is remembered as “space junk,” if it is remembered at all. Cosmosyy is an interactive 3D web game that gives these abandoned NASA objects their stories back. Players choose one of 20 historic missions, covering 6 Apollo landings, 9 Mars missions and 5 deep-space probes, from Apollo 11 to Perseverance and Voyager. They fly the spacecraft, land on lunar and Martian terrain built from NASA elevation data and imagery, and walk the surface in first-person or third-person view. Along the way they discover 113 heritage artifacts, including ALSEP stations, lunar rovers, Surveyor probes, Mars landers and the Pioneer plaque. Each one opens in a holographic inspector with an exploded-view 3D model, archival NASA photographs and NASA NSSDCA catalog data. Each artifact also gets a 6-beat animated story that covers what it was, what it discovered and why it was left behind, told as a first-person “Dormant Voice Log” in English and Hinglish. A Kids mode and an Explorer mode let learners choose between a simple story and a technical, cited one. Every mission ends with a mission report. Cosmosyy turns “discarded equipment” into cultural heritage, helping school-age learners see these objects as historic artifacts worth preserving, and linking Apollo’s legacy to the Artemis missions ahead
details:
Details

Cosmosyy is an interactive 3D web game that tells the stories of the hardware humanity left behind on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. The player picks one of 20 historic NASA missions (6 Apollo landings, 9 Mars missions and 5 deep-space probes), flies the spacecraft, lands at the site and explores it on foot in first-person or third-person view. Each of the 113 abandoned artifacts, from ALSEP stations and lunar rovers to Surveyor probes, Mars landers and the Pioneer plaque, can be scanned and opened in a holographic inspector. There the player can orbit the 3D model, break it into an exploded view, read NASA catalog data and watch a 6-beat animated story about what the object was, what it discovered and why it was left behind. Each artifact speaks in the first person as a Dormant Voice Log, in English or Hinglish. Every mission ends with a report of what the player found. The intended impact is simple: students stop seeing "discarded equipment" as space junk and start seeing it as humanity's first archaeological record beyond Earth, and the Apollo-era stories connect directly to the Artemis missions ahead.

Tech Stack

• React 19, TypeScript (strict) and Vite

• Three.js with React Three Fiber, Drei and Postprocessing for 3D scenes

• Rapier physics and ecctrl character controller for landing and surface exploration

• Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for the interface, Zustand for state, Zod for content validation

• Howler.js and 600+ narration clips in English and Hinglish, i18next for English and Hindi interface text

• Responsive, touch-ready layout with mobile fullscreen controls

• Deployed on Vercel

Innovation Highlights

• Storytelling from the object's point of view: Every artifact narrates its own life in the first person, so history becomes a story and not a fact sheet.

• Play, don't read: Learners fly, land, walk and discover each artifact themselves, then watch its 6-beat story in 3D.

• Two audiences, one game: A Kids mode (simple story) and an Explorer mode (cited technical track) can be switched at any time, and every story is available in English and Hinglish.
